scenes.chapter: THE RULES LIVE ON THE SERVER
MADE FOR YOUR KIND OF PEOPLE

cues.text: Your friends know your name. But how well do they know you?
Could you recognise yourself in someone else’s answers?
I created Who’s Me because I wanted a game to play at friend gatherings.
Something that gets us laughing, talking, and learning more about each other.
One person creates a room. Friends join with a code. No account needed.
Everyone secretly receives another player’s name. Nobody gets their own. Your challenge: think like that friend.
If Alice gets Ben, she chooses what she thinks Ben would choose.
Everyone answers the same multiple-choice questions.
Once all answers are in, the game moves forward together.
Browse your friends’ answers and look for familiar clues.
Then guess who was playing you.
When everyone has guessed, the identities are revealed. A correct guess earns one point.
Behind the game, Flutter connects to Serverpod through a generated Dart client.
The server manages the game, with PostgreSQL storing its state.
Serverpod validates each move and controls when the round advances.
Each player receives a private view, keeping secret identities hidden.
WebSocket streams keep connected players updated as the game progresses.
Saved room state lets players reconnect after a refresh.
The best part comes afterwards: Why did you think I’d choose that?
That’s the goal. A playful reason to understand our friends a little better.
Who’s Me? Think like a friend. Discover how they see you.
